questions.q: What does the summary say you need in order to start a great company?
a: Not even one good idea
One brilliant original idea
A large amount of startup capital
A detailed ten-year plan
questions.why: Lesson 1 argues that visionary firms succeed through constant idea generation, so a single great idea is not required.

questions.q: What two parts make up a company's core ideology?
a: A higher purpose and a set of core values
A mission statement and a memorable logo
A strong leader and loyal employees
A product roadmap and a budget
questions.why: Lesson 2 defines core ideology as a purpose larger than profit combined with values that hold steady over time.

questions.q: Why do visionary companies keep producing great ideas?
a: They generate so many ideas in the first place
They hire consultants to supply ideas
They buy ideas from smaller rivals
They wait for one perfect idea to arrive
questions.why: Lesson 1 says these companies focus on the process of generating ideas in volume, which makes standout ideas likely.

questions.q: What usually happens to new hires who do not share a visionary company's ideology?
a: They leave very quickly
They are promoted into management
They receive extra training
They stay on at lower pay
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the fit is all or nothing, so employees either thrive in the culture or depart soon after joining.

questions.q: How does the summary illustrate Walt Disney enforcing company values?
a: Swearing on the job could get you fired
Employees had to wear formal suits
Staff were expected to work weekends
Managers had to rotate departments
questions.why: Lesson 3 recalls that Disney fired anyone heard using a four-letter word other than love, with no exceptions.
